lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.title: Welcome aboard
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p1.text1: So you mean to go to sea. Good. Keep this book close, hand, for the sea forgives nothing twice and this Almanac holds what every captain before you learned the hard way: how to build a ship and sail her, how to keep a crew alive and willing, how to trade, how to fight, and how to keep clear of the hangman.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p2.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_almanac}**Captain's Almanac** is bound from a book, two pieces of leather and two copper ingots.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p2.list1: Use it in your hand to read it wherever you stand.
Sneak and use it on a table or any surface to lay it down. A placed Almanac lies shut until someone opens it to read.
Turn the pages with the corner arrows, the arrow keys or the mouse wheel. Escape closes the book.
The ribbons on the edge are bookmarks, one per chapter. Hover one to read its name; click it to turn there.
Words in {#2e6a24}green ink{/} are tips worth remembering, and words in {#9a1c14}red ink{/} are warnings you ignore at your peril.
Names in {#2a4580}blue ink{/} lead to another chapter: click one to turn there.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p2.text2: The book remembers where you left off and opens there next time.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p3.text1: Some pages carry a **Show me** button. Press it and the Almanac shows you the thing being done, step by step, on a little model of a ship. Back out of the scene and you return to the same page.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p3.text2: Hover over an item that has a scene, such as the cannon, and hold the Ponder key to watch it from your inventory.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p4.headi: How this book is laid out
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p4.text1: Start with [[pirates_n_ships:first_ship|Your first ship]]: it takes you from a heap of planks to a ship under sail in a few pages. The chapters after it tell each part of the trade in full.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p4.text2: The last pages are for the purser and the quartermaster: [[pirates_n_ships:inventory|The ship's inventory]] lists every block and item with a line on each, [[pirates_n_ships:ledger|The Quartermaster's ledger]] holds the settings and orders a server's keeper needs, and [[pirates_n_ships:not_yet|Not yet charted]] owns up to what is still missing.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.title: Your first ship
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p1.te: Every captain starts the same way: with planks, a helm and more courage than sense. Follow these steps in order and you will be under sail before the sun is down.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p2.sh: Show me: building and assembling a ship
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p2.te: Build a hull of wood floating in the water. Planks, slabs, stairs and glass keep the sea out; a hollow hull with a deck floats high and dry.
Leave a gap of one block to the shore, the quay or any other build. Everything that touches the hull becomes part of the ship.

Natural ground never goes to sea: dirt, sand, raw stone, ore, gravel, ice and leaves stay behind when the ship is launched. Cut and crafted blocks (cobblestone, bricks, logs and planks) sail with her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p3.te: Craft a {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** from four sticks and a plank and place it on the deck. Stand behind it and look the way she should sail: the bow is where the helmsman looks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p4.te: Raise a mast of logs or fences. Across it set two rows of {item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**yards**, the lower one 2 to 8 blocks below the upper. Then place a {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch** anywhere on deck.
Add a {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan** if you want an anchor, and you will.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p5.te: Use the helm. Every block joined to it becomes one ship: she floats, rolls with the sea, and keeps her hold dry.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p6.te: Use the sail winch: furled, then half, then full. The wind fills the canvas and she gathers way.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p7.te: Hold right-click on the helm to take the wheel. Move the mouse, or hold A and D: right or D turns her to starboard, left or A to port. The line above your hotbar shows the rudder. Let go and the wheel stays where you left it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p8.te: Use the capstan to let go the anchor, and again to weigh it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p9.te: Sneak and use the helm with an empty hand to open the ship screen, then press **Disassemble** twice. She must lie nearly still and level first.
That is the whole of it. Now read [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]] to learn what keeps her afloat, and [[pirates_n_ships:sailing|Sailing]] to learn how to make her go where you want.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p10.t: A shipwright will build you a sloop. At a seafarer village, open the harbour master's desk and look at the **Orders** tab. Pay in doubloons, bring the logs and wool he asks for, and come back for her when she is ready. [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]] tells you more.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.title: Ships
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p1.heading: Ships
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p1.text1: A ship is a heap of timber that has agreed to float. Treat her well, know what she can bear, and mend her quickly when she is hurt.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.heading: Launching at the helm
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.show_me: Show me: building and assembling a ship
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.text1: Using a {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** that stands in the world launches a ship:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_1: Every block joined to the helm, face to face or edge to edge, becomes part of her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_2: Air, water and natural ground never join: dirt, sand, raw stone, ores, gravel, ice, snow, leaves, coral and kelp stay where they are. Logs and planks are no ground, so a wooden ship is whole.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_3: A ship may hold up to 2048 blocks. A bigger one the helm refuses, and says so. A dock that touches the hull counts toward the limit, so keep a gap.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_4: Chests and barrels keep what is in them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_5: The sea closes over the place where she was built; no hole is left in the water.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.text2: Your ship gets a name and an owner: you. Use a **name tag** on her helm to rename her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.heading: The ship screen
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.text1: Sneak and use the helm of your own ship with an empty hand to open the ship screen. It has three tabs.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_1: **Ship:** her name (type a new one and press Rename), the flag she flies, her hull (compartments, flooding, breaches, pumps), her load and speed, the anchor, the sails, crew and bunks, the days of supplies left and the last payday. **Disassemble**, pressed twice, takes her apart.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_2: **Crew:** buttons for every whistle order, then every hand aboard with his morale, station, order and pay. **Release** takes a hand off his station; **Dismiss** lets him go.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_3: **Stations:** every station aboard, who works it and what he does. **Man** lists your free hands; pick one with **Send** and he goes there and stays.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.text2: Only the owner opens the screen; others are told she is not their ship. Step more than 8 blocks from the helm and it closes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.heading: Taking her apart
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.text1: Press **Disassemble** twice on the ship screen. She becomes blocks again, set square to the world with her heading turned to the nearest quarter. It is refused when:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.list1_3: something solid is in the way (you are told where).
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.text2: Players and beasts on deck are set down on the deck blocks, and any water inside the hull is let out.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.text3: If her helm is broken she stays a ship: her stations still work, but nothing steers or takes her apart until you place a new helm anywhere on her deck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.heading: The dry hold
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.text1: A ship knows her own hull. Any room that lies below the lowest place water could pour in stays dry: a closed cabin is dry, and an open boat is dry up to her rim. Inside the dry part there is no water: you walk and breathe as on land.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.list1_1: **Watertight:** full blocks, slabs, stairs and glass.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.list1_2: **Not watertight:** fences, walls, bars, panes, ladders and chains.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.list1_3: **Doors, trapdoors and fence gates** are openings: watertight when shut, a way in for water when open.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.text2: The dry volume under the waterline is what keeps her up. Flood water weighs her down, and a ship flooded through is a ship on the bottom.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.heading: Flooding
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text1: A hull block destroyed below the waterline is a breach, and the sea pours into the room behind it. So does an open hatch or door below the waterline. The bigger and deeper the hole, the faster the water comes: a single hole one block under lets in about a block of water every second.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.list1_1: Rooms joined by an open door or hatch fill together. A shut door holds the water back.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.list1_2: Placing any block into the breach stops the flow.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.list1_3: Flood water shows as a level surface in the room, rising and falling with the flood.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text2: Below that surface you hold your breath as in the sea. Get your head clear of the water, or drown in your own hold.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.heading: Pumps
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.text1: Craft a {item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**bilge pump** from a stick, three planks and a bucket. Place it on the hold floor, or on the deck right above the hold: its pipe reaches 4 blocks down through the planks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.text2: Hold right-click on it to pump. It lifts one block of water a second and stops when you let go. Your view tells you how much water is left, or that the bilge is dry. It drains the highest flooded room below it, and several pumps in one room add up.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.text3: Pumping is hard work and makes you hungry. Post a hand at the pump with the whistle and order **Man the pumps**: he pumps until the room is dry.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.heading: Patching a breach
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.show_me: Show me: patching and mending a hull
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:hull_patch}**hull patch** is a tarred plank; two planks and a lump of coal or charcoal make two. Stand inside, look at the edge of the hole (the face of a hull block beside it) and use the patch. It fills the hole and the water stops at once.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.text2: A patch goes only into a real hole in an assembled ship; anywhere else it tells you so and is not spent. You may break a patch later and put in a proper plank, but the hole is open while you swap.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.heading: When she breaks in two
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text1: Shoot or break the only block joining two parts of a ship and she splits. The part with the helm stays your ship; the other becomes a wreck that drifts but no longer sails, and its nameplate reads "Wreck of" her name. Pieces of fewer than four blocks fall apart into items.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text2: You can nail her together again with a {item:pirates_n_ships:shipwright_toolkit}**shipwright's toolkit**: a {item:pirates_n_ships:carpenters_hammer}**carpenter's hammer**, a {item:pirates_n_ships:saw}**saw**, {item:pirates_n_ships:nails}**nails** and leather. Three iron nuggets make eight nails.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text3: **1.** Sneak and use the toolkit on the part you keep, usually the one with the helm. While you hold the toolkit, green sparkles show where the pieces meet.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text4: **2.** Bring the broken piece back against her, lined up straight and touching face to face. Bridge a one-block gap with planks first.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text5: **3.** Use the toolkit on the broken piece. After a moment of hammering it is nailed back on, with its chests and stations, and she keeps her name.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text6: Each repair takes 4 nails. Only pieces of the same ship join, and only pieces of up to 200 blocks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p10.text1: A ship should look the part.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p10.list1_: A {item:pirates_n_ships:nameplate}**nameplate** (any sign and a gold nugget) shows her name once she is launched and named.

A **figurehead** for the bow: a mermaid, lion, eagle or skull, from four planks and a prismarine shard, gold ingot, feather or bone. Click the hull block it should hang on, and the figure looks toward you.
The {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_lantern}**ship's lantern** stands on deck, hangs from a beam or from a bracket on a wall, and burns even under water.
{item:pirates_n_ships:stern_window}**Stern windows** go into a wall from outside; right-click to open or close the shutters.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope_coil}**Rope coils** stack four to a spot.
The {item:pirates_n_ships:chart_table}**chart table** is a captain's table with a chart spread on it.
The {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**sea cot** is a wooden bed for the great cabin. Sleep in it aboard and you lie in it as she sails, and wake and respawn at it wherever she has gone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p11.text1: The shipwrights of the seafarer villages build to order. Open the harbour master's desk and turn to the **Orders** tab: each ship shows her price in doubloons, the days he needs, and the logs and wool he wants. Any logs and any wool will do.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p11.text2: **1.** Carry the doubloons and the materials, and press **Order**. You receive a {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_receipt}**ship receipt**; its tooltip counts the days.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p11.text3: **2.** When it reads "Ready for pickup", use the same port's desk with the receipt in hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p11.text4: **3.** Your ship lies assembled at a free berth beside the pier, and she is yours.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p11.text5: A shipwright builds at most three ships at once. If both berths are taken, come back later: the receipt stays good. Armed sloops are never for sale; you earn one by rank or take one at sea (see [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]] and [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]]).
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.list1_: **Keep near the middle of the world.** Very far from the world's centre, many tens of thousands of blocks out, ships stop moving true.
**Water under the hull.** A ship floats only on the water beneath her own hull; a ship in a dry dock beside the sea stays put.
**Load trims her.** The shipwright ballasts her level as you built her, but cargo and flood water make her list and sit lower.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.title: Sailing
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p1.text1: A ship is only as good as the hand who sails her. Learn the wind, learn your canvas, and learn to keep the bow where you want it. The rest is patience.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text1: Every sea has one wind, the same for every soul on it. It blows from one quarter at a time, between a light air and a fresh gale, and it veers and freshens slowly through the day.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text2: Rain stiffens it by half again, and a thunderstorm more than doubles it and brings sudden gusts.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text3: You can read the wind without instruments. Out on the water, thin white streaks drift past from where it comes, more of them and faster the harder it blows. Flags stream downwind, and set sails belly out to leeward.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text4: Aboard, the compass rose at the bottom of your view carries a pale arrow on the side the wind comes from. The longer the arrow, the stronger the wind; it glows amber in a gust.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.show_: Show me: rigging a sail and working the winch
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text1: A square sail hangs between two {item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**yards**. A yard is a row of yard blocks laid end to end across the mast; its middle block marks the mast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text2: **1.** Set the upper yard across the mast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text3: **2.** Set a second yard of the same direction 2 to 8 blocks straight below it. Between the two middle blocks there may be only air or mast (logs, fences).
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text4: **3.** The pair is now one sail. The cloth is drawn between them; you place no canvas blocks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text5: The sail's area is the yards' mean length times the drop between them: two yards 5 wide and 5 apart give 25. A yard may be up to 15 blocks long. Three yards on one mast make two sails.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text6: A square sail loves a wind from astern and is useless within 45° of the wind.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text7: Click a yard that heads no sail and it tells you what is wrong with the rig.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text1: A triangular sail is rigged with {item:pirates_n_ships:rope}**rope** and three {item:pirates_n_ships:cleat}**cleats**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text2: **1.** Put one cleat high on the side of the mast: the head.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text3: **2.** Put one on the deck or a bowsprit further forward, at least 2 blocks lower: the tack.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text4: **3.** Put one straight below the head: the clew.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text5: **4.** Use a rope on the head cleat, then on the tack cleat, no more than 16 blocks away. The rope is spent and a stay runs between them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text6: The cloth fills the triangle between the stay and the clew. Its area is half of head-to-tack times head-to-clew. A fore-and-aft sail is the one for a wind on the beam: it still drives at 45° off the wind.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text7: Click the head cleat with an empty hand to work its trim. Break the clew and the cloth goes but the stay stays; break the tack and you get your rope back.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text8: A rope between two cleats or mooring rings that is no stay becomes a rope line: a sagging rope for a rail or a rigging. Each cleat or ring holds up to four.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text1: Every sail has three trims: furled, half and full. Half sail draws half the force of full.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.list1: Use the {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch** on deck to work **every** sail of the ship together: furled, then half, then full, then furled again.
Click an upper yard, or the head cleat of a triangular sail, with an empty hand to work that one sail alone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text2: The force grows with the wind you feel on board, the area of the canvas and its trim. No sail drives within 30° of the wind, and a ship running before the wind never outruns it. Sails work only on a ship afloat.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text3: You need not brace the yards: the crew is assumed to trim every sail as well as it can be trimmed. Watch the cloth instead. A sail that draws bellies out to leeward; a sail that shakes and hangs slack is in the no-go zone, and you must bear away.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text4: Your hull holds you on course. A ship slides ahead far more easily than sideways, so a beam wind drives her forward instead of pushing her to leeward. No keel block is needed.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.show_: Show me: steering at the helm
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text1: Hold right-click on the {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** of an assembled ship to take the wheel. Then move the mouse, or hold A and D, to turn it: right or D puts her to starboard, left or A to port. The wheel turns three quarters of a turn each way from midships.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text2: The line above your hotbar shows the rudder angle, up to 35° either side. Let go and the wheel stays where you left it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text3: The rudder bites only while the ship moves through the water, and it works the other way round when she makes sternway. A slow ship turns on the same circle as a fast one; she just takes longer to sail it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text4: If your server has turned off steering by dragging, click the wheel instead: its right third one step to starboard, its left third to port, the middle back to midships.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.text1: Wind on the side of a sail heels the ship over, and the hull rights itself. A wide, shallow hull stands stiffest. As the heel nears 25°, the sails spill their wind, so no storm will lay a sound ship on her side under canvas alone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.text2: The shipwright ballasts every ship as you built her: a tall stern castle or a heavy gun deck on one side does not tip her. What you load later does. Cargo stowed to one side and water in the hold make her list; pump her dry and trim the load, as [[pirates_n_ships:trade|Cargo and trade]] explains.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.text3: A long, wide hull stands steadier than a short, narrow one. Build her with some beam if you mean to carry a press of sail.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.show_: Show me: dropping and weighing anchor
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan** works the anchor. The anchor hangs outside the hull on the capstan's side, just below the deck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.list1: Use the capstan to let go. The anchor sinks fast, with the chain rattling, and lands a few blocks astern if you still had way on.
Once it bites, the chain pulls her up gently at the bow. She swings round toward the capstan's side and lies head to her chain.
She counts as anchored once the anchor holds and she has stopped.
Use the capstan again to weigh: the chain comes in at a steady pace and drags the anchor up to the hull. Use it again midway to let go once more.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.text2: The chain is 32 blocks long. Over deeper water the capstan refuses to let go, for the anchor would find no bottom.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.text3: A ship pulling harder than her anchor holds drags it over the seabed. Furl before you anchor.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text1: There are no mooring lines to belay at a quay: a ship tied up is simply a ship lying still at the berth. Bring her in slowly, drop the anchor, and she is moored. A harbour counts your ship as moored at its port once she lies within about 32 blocks of it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text2: {item:pirates_n_ships:mooring_ring}**Mooring rings** and **cleats** serve the grappling hook. A hook flying close to a ring catches on it, and a hook held by a ring holds twice as far before it tears loose. With your hook set in another ship, use a ring or a cleat on your own ship to make the rope fast there; the ships keep hauling together and you can walk away. A ring on land holds a hooked ship the same way. The [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]] chapter tells the rest of the hook.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p10.head: Waves and weather
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p10.text: The sea follows the weather. In fair weather there is a low swell or a light chop; in rain the sea runs rough; in a thunderstorm the crests stand two blocks and more above the still water. The change comes over about a minute.
Waves come in sets: a run of bigger seas, then a calmer spell. Your ship rises on the crests and sinks in the troughs, a small boat far more than a big one, and in heavy weather the bow throws spray.

A rowing boat rides the swell too, climbing the same crests out on open water, and anything you throw overboard bobs along with it; on lakes, rivers and in the shallows by the shore the water lies still as ever.
In rough seas every open hatch or low rim near the waterline takes water at the crests. Close your hatches and keep a pump manned before a storm.
A moving ship leaves a wake: a bow wave spreading from the stem and a trail of foam astern that fades over some seconds.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.head: Ratlines
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.text: {item:pirates_n_ships:ratlines}**Ratlines** are rope nets for climbing aloft, to a crow's nest or a yard.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.list: Click the side of a mast to hang a net on it like a ladder.
Click the top of the deck or the gunwale to lay a sloped net instead. It rises at 45° the way you face, so stand at the gunwale looking at the mast.
Click a ratline you placed to add the next one at the end of its run, straight up a hanging net or up and forward along a sloped one.
Sneak to place against the clicked side instead.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.text: Climb a hanging net like a ladder; walk up a sloped one. A net needs something to rest on: break one and the nets that hung from it fall too. A sloped run may end on a yard right beside the mast, and from there you climb straight on up the hanging net above.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p12.head: The ship's bell
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p12.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:ships_bell}**ship's bell** sits on a post or a wall. Right-click it and it swings and rings.
It is a bell and nothing more: it does not call your crew. But mark it when you lie in a harbour: when raiders come, every bell in the settlement rings the alarm.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.head: The crow's nest
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**crow's nest** is a barrel for the masthead. Place it on a log, a fence, a wall or any block with a solid top; if that block goes, the nest falls. Climb up the mast and step in over the rim, and sneak to stay put.
Whoever stands in the nest keeps the lookout, you or a hand you post there with the whistle. Every few seconds the lookout sweeps 160 blocks around the ship and calls what is new to everyone aboard:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.list: **Sail ho!** A ship, by the flag she flies: merchant, navy, pirate, a wreck, or just a ship.
**Land ho!** The nearest coast, once per stretch of shore.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.text: Bearings are called in points of the compass from the bow: dead ahead, two points off the starboard bow, on the beam, abaft the beam, dead astern. A full circle is 32 points. The lookout calls each sighting once and remembers it a while after it drops from view.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.head: The ship's panels
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.text: While you are aboard, two small panels watch over her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.list: **The compass,** bottom left: a ship-shaped needle points along your heading, the wind arrow sits outside the rose, and below it you read the speed in knots and the rudder angle.
**The hull strip,** bottom right: one cell per compartment from bow to stern, filling blue as water comes in, with a red mark at a breach and a pump sign where a pump works.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.text: They stay while you walk the deck, climb the rigging or stand at the helm, and go a moment after you leave her. Her name, load and crew are on the ship screen at the helm; see [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p15.head: Music at sea
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p15.text: Aboard, the next tune is a sea shanty; at sea but not aboard, an air of wind and water. A tune is never cut off, and a few minutes of quiet pass between them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.title: Crew
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.heading: Crew
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.text1: One captain cannot work the winch, the helm, the pumps and the guns at once. A crew can. Hire good hands, feed them, pay them and give them a dry place to sleep, and they will sail your ship for you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.heading: Hiring hands
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text1: Every harbour master's desk has a **Crew** tab. Each day a port has a few souls looking for a berth: sailors at seafarer villages, pirates at pirate islands, navy ratings at navy outposts. Each asks a one-time fee and then a daily wage.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_1: A sailor asks 10 doubloons, a navy rating 15, a pirate 20.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_2: Villagers will not sign on with a captain they refuse to trade with.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_3: Pirates sign on only with a friend of the pirates or a captain of some infamy, a Buccaneer or worse.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_4: Navy ratings sign on only with an enlisted officer.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text2: Before you hire, bring your own ship in and lie within about 32 blocks of the port. The new hand walks straight aboard and waits on deck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text3: Every hand needs a free {item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**hammock**. Hang more hammocks before you take on more crew; the desk refuses a hand you cannot bunk.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.heading: Stations
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text1: A station is a block a hand can work: the {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch**, the **helm**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**bilge pump**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:cannon}**cannon**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**crow's nest**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text2: A hand at a station stays at his post while the ship sails and turns. He walks there across the deck, even under way, and the station starts its work only when he has arrived. If he cannot reach it, or has not got there after ten seconds, he is put there anyway.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text3: A hand leaves his station when it is broken, when the ship is taken apart, or when he dies.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.heading: The captain's whistle
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** is how a captain speaks to his crew.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_1: Use it on a hand, then on a station: he takes that station and stays there.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_2: Use it on a hand at a station: he is released.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_3: Sneak and use it on a hand to dismiss him from your service. Only you, or whoever hired him, may do so.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_4: Use it in the air to open the order wheel. Point at an order and click, or hold the use key, aim and let go. Escape closes the wheel.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text2: The orders on the wheel: **Hoist sails**, **Reef sails**, **Furl sails**, **Man the pumps**, **Fire!**, **Load!**, **Fire at will**, **Drop anchor**, **Weigh anchor** and **Release crew**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text3: No whistle in your sea chest? The ship screen at the helm gives every one of these orders too, and assigns, releases and dismisses hands. See [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.heading: Orders, not assignments
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text1: You need not post every hand yourself. Blow an order and every unmanned station that can carry it out becomes an open job. Free hands on deck take the nearest one by themselves within a second, get to work and stay there afterwards. A hand you posted yourself stays put and is never moved.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text2: A hand answers in chat ("Aye, hoisting the sails!") and then works. Each step of trim takes him two seconds; the sails change when the work is done.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text3: If nobody can carry an order out, you are told why: no ship under you, no station aboard that takes it, nothing to do, or what is wrong with the rig. If every hand is busy you hear "No free hands", and the job waits for the next hand who comes aboard.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text4: **Release crew** sends every hand off his station, ends **Fire at will** and cancels the open jobs.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.heading: A helmsman
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.text1: Post a hand at the helm and he keeps her steady. He turns the wheel toward the course he is given and puts the rudder midships when he arrives ("We've arrived, captain! Rudder midships"). He does not touch the sails: order **Hoist sails** as well.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.text2: Take the wheel yourself at any time and he lets go; release it and he steers on. If the ship stops making headway with her sails set, he tells you she is stuck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.heading: Meals
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text1: Twice a day, at noon and at sunset, the hands who are off duty sit down by the {item:pirates_n_ships:pantry}**pantry** (or the water barrel) and eat for a few seconds. An order gets them up at once.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text2: The meal is a sight to see, nothing more: the crew's rations are taken once a day, at dawn. What they eat and drink, and what happens when the pantry runs dry, is in [[pirates_n_ships:provisions|Provisions]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.heading: Hammocks and rest
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text1: Hang a {item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**hammock** between two supports at the same height, such as fence posts, walls, logs or the hull side: click the block next to one support while looking toward the other.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text2: At nightfall every hand who is not at a station turns in to the nearest free hammock and gets up at dawn. A night in a hammock lifts his morale; a night aboard without a free hammock lowers it, and he will grumble. Hands on watch all night are not affected, and an order at night gets sleepers up at once. Each hammock is one bunk.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text3: You may sleep in one too, on land or aboard: right-click a free one at night and you lie in it as in a bed. Aboard you stay in it while she sails, you count toward skipping the night, and the dawn puts you on your feet beside it. Sleeping there sets your respawn point, and aboard that point sails with the ship.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text4: The captain sleeps in a {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**sea cot**, a wooden bed for the great cabin, which works the same way at sea.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.heading: Morale
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text1: Every hand has a morale between 0 and 100; a new hand comes aboard at 70. You read it on the ship screen, or by using the whistle on him.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_1: A night in a hammock: a little up. A night without one: down by ten.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_2: Paid on time: up by one. Unpaid: down by eight.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_3: Hungry: down by ten a day. Thirsty: down by twenty-five a day.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_4: A ration of rum: up a little each day.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_5: Scurvy: down every day until it is cured.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text2: Hungry hands work at three quarters of their speed, thirsty hands at half.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.heading: Wages and desertion
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text1: Every dawn each hand wants 2 doubloons. The pay comes from the chests, barrels and cargo crates aboard, the ones nearest the helm first, and the lowest in spirits are paid first. If the coin aboard runs short, the rest comes out of your own purse while you are at sea in that world.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text2: A hand whose morale stays below 20 for two dawns means to desert. He tells you so and walks off at the next port the ship comes within 48 blocks of, or wherever she is after three more dawns. Feed him, pay him and lift his spirits above 20 again, and he changes his mind.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text3: On some seas a whole crew that stays miserable for three dawns rises in mutiny, turns pirate and takes the ship from you. Your server tells you whether yours is such a sea.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.heading: Fire at will
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text1: Order **Fire at will** and your gun crews take over their cannons. Each crew lays its gun on the nearest hostile ship within its arc and 64 blocks, leads a moving target, loads from the powder and shot nearby and fires when the shot will tell.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text2: Who is hostile depends on your own flag:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_1: Under the navy flag: the Jolly Roger, and ships whose false colours are found out.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_2: Under the Jolly Roger: navy ships, merchants and unflagged ships.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_3: Under a merchant flag or none: only the Jolly Roger.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text3: Nobody fires on a ship that has struck her colours, and your crew holds fire if you strike yours. A cannon cannot turn sideways, so turn the ship to bring the guns to bear. **Release crew** ends it. The guns themselves are in [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.title: Flags
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.heading: Flags
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.text1: A flag is a promise. It tells every ship on the horizon who you are and what you mean to do, and the sea holds you to it. Choose your colours with care, and know what it costs to lie with them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.heading: The colours
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_1: {item:pirates_n_ships:merchant_flag}**Merchant flag** (a stick, two white wool, red dye), or no flag at all: neutral to everyone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_2: {item:pirates_n_ships:navy_flag}**Navy flag** (a stick, two blue wool, white dye): the navy and the merchants are friends, the pirates foes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_3: {item:pirates_n_ships:jolly_roger_flag}**Jolly Roger** (a stick, two black wool, a bone): the pirates are friends, the navy hunts you, and merchants may strike to you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_4: **Any banner:** your own flag, neutral to all. The cloth shows the banner's colour and every one of its patterns.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.heading: The flagpole
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**flagpole** is three sticks stood on end; it makes two. The flag hangs downwind from its top, a block high and a block and a half long, so leave it room.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.list1_1: **Use it with a flag:** the flag runs up the pole and flies after three seconds; you get the old one back.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.list1_2: **Use it with an empty hand:** strike the colours (the flag comes down but stays on the pole), or raise them again.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.list1_3: **Sneak and use it with an empty hand:** take the flag down into your hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.text2: Stack flagpoles to raise one tall pole, up to 6 blocks. The top flies the flag, and you may work it from any block of the pole. Placing a pole on top takes the flag up with it; breaking one in the middle splits it in two, and the upper part keeps the flag.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.heading: What your flag tells the law
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.text1: A ship flies the highest flag on her poles.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_1: **Under the Jolly Roger** the navy fires on everyone aboard on sight, and being seen under it is a crime. Pirates let you be.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_2: **Under the navy flag** you pass the navy, as long as your record is clean and the navy thinks well of you. A suspect who flies it may be found out by any navy soldier in sight. Then you are charged heavily, and the navy hunts your ship for five minutes whatever she flies.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_3: A navy ship with a manned crow's nest sees your flag half again as far and sees through it half again as fast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.text2: Firing on a ship that has struck her colours, or on one under a merchant flag or a banner, is a crime. If your crew fires, the charge is yours as her owner.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.heading: Striking your colours
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.text1: Strike your flag and you surrender: the navy and the pirates stop attacking. A navy patrol that sees you strike holds its fire, keeps you in sight for half a minute and sails on. Raise the Jolly Roger again and the chase is back on. The [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]] chapter tells you what your crimes cost.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.heading: Banners and dyed sails
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text1: Hoist any banner on a flagpole to fly your own flag: the cloth takes the banner's colour and patterns, its top edge at the pole.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text2: Your canvas can carry colour too.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.list1_1: Use a **dye** on the upper yard of a square sail, or the head cleat of a triangular one: the whole cloth takes the colour, and one dye is spent. White dye brings back the plain canvas.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.list1_2: A large square sail can carry a **banner**: use the banner on its upper yard. The cloth takes the banner's colour with its patterns drawn upright over it. Both yards must be at least 3 blocks long and 2 blocks apart.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.list1_3: Sneak and use the yard with an empty hand to take the banner back; breaking the yard block that holds it drops it. While a banner hangs, dyes are refused. Triangular sails take dye only.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text3: Colours are only for show: they never change what a sail does, and they stay through launching, taking apart and every change of trim.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.title: Provisions
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p1.te: An empty pantry sinks more ships than cannon ever did. Every dawn your crew eats and drinks one day's provisions from the stores aboard. Keep the stores full and the crew stays willing; let them run dry and you will soon be sailing alone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p2.te: The {item:pirates_n_ships:pantry}**pantry** (eight planks around a sheaf of wheat) is the ship's food store: 27 slots that open like a chest. Its doors face you when you place it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p2.li: Anything edible counts, by how filling it is. One hand needs about a loaf of bread and a bit each day.
The crew eats what will spoil first, and turns up its nose at rotten flesh, spider eyes and other foul fare.
Sneak and use it with both hands empty to read what it holds and what spoils next.
A hopper can only put provisions in, and only takes out what is no provision: empty bottles, bowls, rotten flesh. A hopper below makes a fine waste chute.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p3.te: Fresh food spoils after five days in the pantry and turns to rotten flesh.
Preserved food never spoils: bread, cookies, dried kelp, honey bottles, golden carrots and golden apples, and the sailor's own:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p3.li: {item:pirates_n_ships:hardtack}**Hardtack:** three wheat and a water bucket make two.
{item:pirates_n_ships:salted_fish}**Salted fish:** a cod or salmon and dried kelp.
{item:pirates_n_ships:salt_pork}**Salt pork:** a porkchop and dried kelp.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p4.te: A {item:pirates_n_ships:water_barrel}**water barrel** holds 16 rations of fresh water, and each hand drinks one a day. It is crafted full from planks, iron nuggets and a water bucket.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p4.li: A water bucket pours in 3 rations, a bottle 1. An empty bucket draws 3 out, a glass bottle 1.
Rain slowly fills a barrel that stands under the open sky.
The top shows how full it is, and a broken barrel keeps its water.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p4.te: Water and rum count wherever they are stowed, in a pantry or a barrel.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p5.te: A crew short of food loses heart by the day and works at three quarters of its pace. A crew short of water loses heart far faster and works at half. Both together are a ship of the half-dead. Low spirits end in desertion; see [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]].
After eight days without fresh food, scurvy sets in: the crew weakens and loses heart every day. Any fresh food cures it, and fruit best of all: apples, melon, berries.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p6.te: {item:pirates_n_ships:rum}**Rum** is made from sugar cane, two sugar and a glass bottle. While there is rum aboard, every hand gets a ration a day and his spirits rise for it.
You may drink it yourself: it warms you through for two minutes and leaves the bottle.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p7.te: Swimming or wading in frozen or cold seas and frozen rivers chills you like powder snow: after some seven seconds you are frozen and take hurt.
You are safe in a boat, on deck or in a dry hold, in any piece of leather armour, or with a bottle of rum in you. Swimming anywhere makes you hungry half again as fast as it otherwise would.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p8.te: Prisoners in your brig eat and drink too, half a hand's share, and get no rum. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.title: Cargo and trade
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p1.heading: Cargo and trade
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p1.text1: Buy where a thing is cheap, carry it where it is wanted, and sell it dear. That is the whole of honest trade, and a fine living it makes for a captain with a sound hold and a steady nerve.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.heading: Crates and barrels
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.text1: Bulk cargo goes in containers that hold **one kind of item** in great amounts.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.list1_1: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_crate}**Cargo crate** (four planks and four sticks): 32 stacks of one item.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.list1_2: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_barrel}**Cargo barrel** (six planks and two iron nuggets): 1536 items of one kind, whatever their stack size; best for rum and other small stacks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.text2: Use one with a stack to put it in, with an empty hand to take a stack out, and sneak-use with an empty hand to put in everything of that kind you carry. Items that do not stack are refused, and stolen and clean goods of the same kind never share a container. A broken container keeps its cargo, and hoppers work on it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.heading: Weight and trim
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.text1: Cargo weighs. Crates, cargo barrels, pantries and water barrels grow heavier as they fill: a full crate weighs as much as forty planks. A chest presses down where it stands, so a heavy chest in the bow trims her by the head.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.text2: Spread heavy cargo and keep it low and amidships. A laden ship sits deeper, floods sooner through a breach, and is slower to gather way and to turn.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.text3: The ship screen at the helm reads her load: Light, Laden, Heavily laden or Overloaded.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.heading: The sea chest
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_chest}**sea chest** (three leather over iron, a chest and iron) holds 54 stacks and keeps them when broken, carried or floated.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.list1_1: Use it in the air to carry it on your back. You cannot jump, sprint or swim, you walk slower, and in water it drags you under.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.list1_2: Place it on water and it floats, drifting with wind and current.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.list1_3: Use it to open it, sneak-use to pick it up, or strike it to knock it loose as an item.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:paddle}**paddle** (two planks and a stick) turns a floating chest into a boat of sorts: use the paddle on it to sit on the lid, then paddle forward and back and turn left and right. Sneak to get off. You cannot open the chest while you sit on it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.heading: Doubloons
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.text1: The gold {item:pirates_n_ships:doubloon}**doubloon** is the coin of the sea. Nobody mints it; you earn it:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_1: by selling goods at a harbour master's desk,
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_2: from the purses of slain pirates and pirate captains,
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_3: from the chests of wrecks and buried treasure,
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_4: from bounties, ransoms, delivery contracts, quests and prize money.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.text2: Carry them in your inventory; that is where the markets take them from.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.heading: Harbours
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.text1: The coast has three kinds of port, each with a harbour master's desk.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.list1_1: **Seafarer villages** stand on beaches: a stone quay with the harbour master's hut, a pier with two berths, cottages, a tavern and a shipwright's shed.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.list1_2: **Navy outposts** are stone forts on beaches, rarer than villages: a sea gate, a quay with two berths, cannon on the walls and a garrison that never leaves its posts. An officer stands by the office door.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.list1_3: **Pirate islands** are camps on beaches, rarer still: a jetty, tents, a tavern, a captain's hut and a fence's shack under the Jolly Roger. Strangers are not welcome.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.text2: A desk you place inside a port joins that port.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.heading: The harbour master
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.text1: Every desk has a harbour master behind it, in a green frock coat and a peaked cap. Right-click him, or the {item:pirates_n_ships:harbor_desk}**harbour master's desk**, to open the port's market. If you strike him he waves you off for a while; if he dies, a new one takes the post after three days.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.list1_1: **Goods:** every good the port trades, with your doubloons. Green goods are made here and cheap to buy; orange goods are wanted here and good to sell. Pick a quantity, then Buy or Sell; the prices shown are for the whole quantity.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.list1_2: **Contracts:** delivery offers and the contracts you hold.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.list1_5: **Crew:** hands looking for a berth; see [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.text3: Stay within 8 blocks of the desk, or the market closes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.heading: Prices
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.text1: Buying raises a price and selling lowers it, and prices drift back toward their usual level day by day. Buying and selling in one port always loses money; carrying a good from a port that makes it to a port that wants it pays, though less with every stack you sell.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.text2: The goods of the sea: sugar, fish, timber, iron, grain, hides, cocoa, gunpowder, {item:pirates_n_ships:tobacco}**tobacco**, {item:pirates_n_ships:spices}**spices**, {item:pirates_n_ships:cloth}**cloth** and rum. Spices fetch the most. Tropical ports grow sugar, cocoa, tobacco and spices; colder ports deal in fish, timber and iron; navy outposts sell powder.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.text3: Merchant convoys sail the lanes between the ports and move prices too: a port a convoy has just supplied pays a little less for what she brought.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p9.heading: Stolen goods
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p9.text1: Goods taken from a captured or sunk ship carry a plunder mark in their tooltip. Only a pirate fence buys them, at a heavy discount and with no questions. The desk's sell toggle chooses whether you sell clean or plundered stacks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p9.text2: A village or navy harbour master turns plunder away and reports you to the navy. And the navy looks into your hold: sail within sight of its soldiers or a fort with more than 16 marked goods aboard, under any flag, and you are suspected of piracy. Fence your plunder before you go near the navy.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p10.text1: A navy outpost charges a small docking fee of 5 doubloons when your ship ties up at a berth or anchors inside it, once a day per ship. It comes from your purse, or from the coin in your ship's chests. Leave it unpaid and the outpost's desk will not trade with you until you settle it, coin in hand. Captains the navy trusts well, and officers from Lieutenant up, dock for free. Sailing through costs nothing.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p11.text1: A port offers delivery contracts: carry an amount of a good to another port by a deadline for a reward. Accepting costs a deposit of a fifth of the reward; delivering at the far port's desk pays the reward and gives the deposit back. You may hold three at a time.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p12.text1: Every desk offers up to three quests, renewed every two days. Accept up to three at once; each must be done within five days.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p12.list1_: **Hunts:** pirates, sharks or, rarely, the kraken; or a pirate island's named captain.
**Cargo runs:** a contract with a raised reward and no deposit.
**Treasure hunts:** you get a treasure map; open the chest at the X.
**Escorts:** keep within 96 blocks of a merchant ship on at least half her course and see her into port.
**Raids and patrols:** pirate islands want convoys plundered or navy patrols sunk; navy outposts want pirate ships sunk or taken.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p12.text2: A quest pays doubloons and raises your standing with whoever gave it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.title: Law
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.heading: Law
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.text1: The Crown keeps a ledger on every soul at sea, and on every beast that bites. Steal, strike or sail under false colours and your name goes in it. Stay honest and the navy is your friend; turn pirate and you had better be fast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.heading: Your record
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text1: Every crime adds to your record:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_1: Theft from a village chest, or striking a villager: 5.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_2: Striking the navy, or being seen under the Jolly Roger: 10.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_3: Attacking a neutral ship, press-ganging a prisoner, or being caught with plunder aboard: 15.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_4: Offering stolen goods at a village or navy desk: 17.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_5: Killing a villager: 20. Killing a navy man: 30.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_6: Caught under false colours, or firing on a ship that struck: 40.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.list1_7: Piracy (taking a ship): 50. Deserting the navy: 60.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text2: From 10 you are a **suspect**, from 50 **wanted**, and from 200 **notorious**. Five minutes after your last crime your record begins to fade, by 10 a day.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text3: Theft counts only when someone sees it: a villager, a trader or a navy man nearby. Putting things into a chest is no crime.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.heading: Fines
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.text1: Hold doubloons and right-click a navy officer to pay your fine: 3 doubloons a point, as many whole points as you can afford. He will not deal with a wanted man, and no coin buys a pardon for the notorious.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.heading: Bounties
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.text1: At a record of 50 the navy puts a price on your head of twice your record. It grows as your record grows and is withdrawn once the record falls below 25.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.text2: Kill someone with a price on their head and a {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**bounty proof** lands in your pack. Right-click a navy officer with it to collect. Bring the quarry in alive and it pays half again as much. A claim wipes the quarry's record clean.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.heading: The notice board
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:notice_board}**notice board** (planks and paper) lists every bounty: who is wanted, for how much, who placed it and when, and whether there is one on you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.text2: To place a bounty of your own, type a name, enter at least 10 doubloons and press **Place**. The coin comes out of your pack.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.heading: Shackles and prisoners
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:shackles}**Shackles** (two iron ingots and a chain) take a beaten foe alive.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_1: Use them on a creature at a quarter of its health or less: it becomes your prisoner. It stops fighting and never wanders off. Bosses cannot be taken, and players only where the server allows it and they carry a bounty.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_2: Use them on your prisoner to lead it, or to let go. A led prisoner follows like a beast on a lead.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_3: A prisoner left alone outside a cell tries to slip away.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.heading: Turning in prisoners
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text1: Walk up to a navy officer with your prisoners close by and right-click him with an empty hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.list1_1: A prisoner with a bounty pays half again the bounty; a pirate earns a reward besides.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.list1_2: A shackled navy man or merchant can be ransomed back the same way.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text2: Hold the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** and right-click a shackled sailor on your own ship to press-gang him into your crew. He comes aboard sullen, and it is a crime. Sneak and right-click your own prisoner with an empty hand to set him free.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.heading: The brig
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_bars}**Brig bars** connect like iron bars. The {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_door}**brig door** locks with a {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_key}**brig key** (an iron ingot over an iron nugget): use the key on the door to lock it, and again to unlock it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text2: Any key opens any brig door. Keep your keys away from your prisoners.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text3: A locked door opens only for the one who placed it, and ignores redstone. A prisoner standing in a closed space of at most 64 blocks, walled by solid blocks, bars and a locked brig door, is **in a cell** and does not try to escape, unless your crew's spirits sink so low that the watch grows careless.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.heading: The three powers
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text1: The sea has three powers: the navy, the pirates and the merchants. Their quarrels rise and cool with every deed done at sea, and when the navy and the pirates are at each other's throats there are more patrols, more hunting and more raids.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text2: Each power remembers you, from −100 to 100: the navy, the pirates and the villagers.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.list1_1: Killing pirates pleases the navy. Killing navy men, plundering merchants and selling to fences wins the pirates over. Trading at villages pleases the villagers.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.list1_2: Good standing gets you better prices; bad standing worse. Villagers stop trading with you at −60.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.list1_3: Pirates leave you be once they like you well enough, until you strike first. Fall to −60 with the navy and it fires on sight.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.heading: Navy patrols
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.text1: The navy sends patrols between its outposts and out toward the pirate islands. A patrol keeps a lookout of some 256 blocks and gives chase to any ship under the Jolly Roger, any whose false colours it has seen through, and any whose captain is wanted or carries a bounty of 50 doubloons or more.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.text2: It circles you at about 20 blocks while its guns fire. Strike your colours and it falls silent. Outrun it and it gives up the chase.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.heading: Careers
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text1: There are two ladders, and you may climb only one.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.list1_1: **The navy.** Talk to a navy officer with an empty hand and enlist once the navy trusts you: a good name with it, no bounty and no friends among the pirates. Pirates killed, prisoners brought in, navy quests and a growing name promote you: Midshipman, Lieutenant, Captain, Commodore, Admiral. Firing on the navy or a merchant in service is desertion.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.list1_2: **Infamy.** Plunder fenced, ships taken and a name among the pirates make you a Buccaneer, a Dread Captain and at last a Pirate Lord. A known pirate is never taken into the navy.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.list1_3: **Letter of marque.** Not ready to serve? Buy one from a navy officer for 200 doubloons once the navy thinks well of you. Every pirate you kill under it earns prize money.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text2: Rank has its rewards. A Lieutenant flies the navy flag by right, docks free at navy outposts and receives the officer's bicorne, a saber and the officer's coat, breeches and boots. A navy Captain receives a {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**ship commission** for an armed navy sloop; a Dread Captain is granted a pirate sloop at a pirate island's fence. A navy Captain may also order any ship at a navy outpost's desk for less than the villages ask.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text3: Your title rides before your name in chat and over your head, and before your ship's name when you name her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.title: Weapons and combat
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p1.text1: Sooner or later someone will want your ship, your cargo or your head. Learn the blade, the pistol and the great guns, and learn them before you need them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text1: Three blades are worth carrying, each with its own temper:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.list1_: {item:pirates_n_ships:rapier}**Rapier** (two iron ingots and a stick): light and long, made for the thrust.
{item:pirates_n_ships:cutlass}**Cutlass** (three iron ingots and a stick): heavy and wide, made for the slash.
{item:pirates_n_ships:saber}**Saber** (two iron ingots, a gold ingot and a stick): the officer's blade, good at both.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text2: With one of these in hand the mouse fights differently:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.list2_: **Slash:** a quick left click. A wide, short arc after a brief wind-up.
**Thrust:** hold left click a moment and release. Narrow, longer reach, harder, but slow to recover if it misses.

**Guard:** hold right click. It stops every blow from the front, but each blow costs stamina, the heavier the dearer. When you cannot pay, your guard breaks and you stagger. Blows from behind or the side ignore your guard.

**Parry:** a quick tap of right click just before a blow lands. The blow glances off, the attacker staggers, and for a second you may **riposte** for extra harm. A parry at nothing costs stamina and locks your parry for a moment.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text3: Your stamina shows as a brass-framed bar while you hold a sword. Attacks, guarding and missed parries drain it; it refills when you rest. With an empty bar you can neither guard nor parry.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text4: While you hold one of these swords, right click belongs to the blade. Put it away to open a door or take the helm.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p3.text1: Pirates fight with the same swordplay you do. Watch for the raised arm before a slash, or the arm drawn back before a thrust, and parry just before the blow. A pirate sometimes feints: he stops his swing to bait an early parry and strikes while your guard is spent. Navy officers are skilled duellists with the saber.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:pistol}**pistol** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:musket}**musket** (each two iron ingots, a flint and a plank) are single-shot flintlocks. The musket hits harder and flies flatter and truer; the pistol scatters.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text2: **1.** **Load:** with {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**lead shot** (two iron nuggets make four) and gunpowder in your pack, hold right click: three seconds for the pistol, five for the musket. Let go early and nothing is lost.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text3: **2.** **Aim:** with a loaded gun, hold right click. After a second of steady aim the shot is tighter, and the musket draws your eye in a little.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text4: **3.** **Fire:** left click, while aiming or from the hip. From the hip the ball scatters wide.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text5: Letting go of right click never fires; the gun stays loaded. Sneak to lower an aimed gun. A loaded gun shows a full gold bar in your hotbar and says "Loaded" in its tooltip.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text6: In the rain a quarter of your shots misfire with a click; the charge stays in.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.show_m: Show me: loading and firing a cannon
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:cannon}**cannon** is cast from two iron ingots and a block of iron on a carriage of two logs and a plank. Click the deck block where the **front** of the carriage should stand: the rear takes the block toward you and the barrel overhangs one block ahead, so click the spot by the rail. Both halves need a block beneath them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text2: **1.** **Load:** use it with gunpowder, then with a {item:pirates_n_ships:cannonball}**cannonball** (four iron ingots make two). Powder first, always.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text3: **2.** **Aim:** sneak and use it with an empty hand. The upper half of the block raises the barrel, the lower half lowers it, from 5° down to 20° up in steps of 5°.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text4: **3.** **Fire:** use it with an empty hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text5: The barrel needs five seconds to cool before fresh powder goes in. A ball hits hard and smashes the wooden block it strikes; a hole below a ship's waterline lets the sea in. A ball that grazes a hull at a shallow angle glances off; a square hit does the most harm. From a moving ship the shot carries her speed, and each shot pushes your ship back a little.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text6: A cannon cannot turn sideways. Lay your ship so her broadside bears.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p6.text1: Both load like a cannonball, after the powder.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p6.list1_: {item:pirates_n_ships:chain_shot}**Chain shot** (two iron ingots and a chain make two): two balls on a chain. It flies slower and shorter than a ball, breaks no hull and rips through rigging. Through a square sail it tears the cloth, so the sail draws only with what is left; it cuts ropes and stays and breaks ratlines. Torn cloth mends by itself, a block a minute.

{item:pirates_n_ships:grapeshot}**Grapeshot** (eight iron nuggets in a string-tied bag make two): bursts from the muzzle as nine pellets in a narrow cone. Each pellet hurts whoever it hits and breaks nothing, and none strike your own deck. Fire it across a crowded enemy deck before you board.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p7.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** (three iron ingots over a stick) mounts on a fence, a wall, iron or brig bars, or any full block.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p7.text2: Load it with gunpowder, then a cannonball. Hold right click with an empty hand: the gun follows your eye while you hold, and fires when you let go. It hits less hard and less far than a cannon, breaks no planks and is ready again in three seconds. Sneak and use it to hear what it needs.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text1: Post a hand at a gun with the whistle. Put gunpowder and shot in a chest, barrel or cargo crate within 4 blocks of the gun on the same ship, then blow **Load!**. On **Fire!** every manned, loaded gun goes off ("Aye, firing!"), and the crew reloads by itself from the supply, so a manned gun keeps firing as fast as it cools.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text2: **Fire at will** lets the crews choose their own targets; see [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:grappling_hook}**grappling hook** (three iron ingots and a string) bites into whatever it strikes: another ship, your own ship, or the land.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.list1_: **Throw it:** right click. Its rope reaches 32 blocks.
**Shoot it:** put the hook in your off hand and a musket in your main hand. Hold use to load it into the musket (a full reload and a gunpowder), aim and fire. Its rope reaches 64 blocks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text2: It slips off water, leaves and glass panes, and from creatures, and comes back after two seconds. Throwing a second hook frees the first. Sneak and use with an empty hand to let go. The rope parts if it is stretched past its length.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.list2_: **Hooked into another ship from your own:** the rope hauls both ships together until they lie side by side.
**Haul by hand:** with the rope in hand, hold sneak and its length freezes. Walk back and it pulls the ship toward you.
**Climb:** right-click your own rope while it is in your hand and you go up it hand over hand, when the hook is at least two blocks above you.
**Make fast:** use a cleat or mooring ring of your own while your hook is out, and the rope is tied there.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text1: Once your rope is made fast to a cleat or ring, look at it and use it: you hang from it and slide down to its lower end, riding along as both ships move. Sneak to let go. From your masthead down onto an enemy deck is the classic way across.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text2: Or lay a {item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**boarding plank** (three wooden slabs over two iron nuggets). With the ships alongside, use it on the top of your gunwale facing the other ship. A plank up to four blocks long runs out level and hooks onto her deck, which may sit a block higher or lower. Keep the ships together: if they drift more than a block and a half apart, the plank breaks and drops back to you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.text1: Ships sail the sea lanes between the ports even when no one is watching, and when you come within sight of one she is there: a merchantman with goods in her hold and a few armed sailors, a navy patrol, or a pirate under the Jolly Roger. Navy and pirate sloops carry four guns, loaded, and a shot locker by the mast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.list1: Take goods from a merchant's hold while you stand aboard her, and you have plundered her.
Sink her, and the deed is yours if your shot was the last to strike her.
Kill every fighter aboard and hold her deck for a few seconds, and she is yours, crew and all.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.text2: Taking a merchant is piracy in the navy's eyes. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.list1: **Pirates,** in dark coats and bandanas, attack you and the navy on sight. They drop doubloons and now and then a cutlass.
**Navy soldiers,** in blue coats with white cross belts, carry muskets. They leave you be unless you are wanted; then they keep their distance, aim and fire. They drop lead shot and gunpowder.
**Navy officers,** in gold-trimmed coats, are deadly with the saber.
**Sailors** never fight; they run from danger.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.text1: Pirates and the navy fight each other wherever they meet. Striking or killing navy men is a crime; killing pirates is not.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text1: Every pirate island has a captain, a named villain with a standing bounty of 300 doubloons on every notice board. He is a dangerous swordsman.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text2: To fight him alone, sneak and use him with a sword in hand. If he accepts, his crew keeps out of the duel unless you strike them. The duel ends when one of you falls, when you run, or after five minutes. Strike him first and he refuses: there is no honour in it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text3: Slain, he drops his hat, maybe his coat, breeches and boots, a purse of doubloons, a treasure map of his island and your bounty proof. Taken alive in shackles, he pays better still. Five days after his fall a successor takes his place. Now and then he puts to sea in his own ship, and if you carry a letter of marque or a bounty proof, he hunts you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p14.text1: Linger long at a navy outpost or a seafarer village and the pirates take notice. One day the cry goes up, "Sails on the horizon!", and the bells ring. Pirate sloops come in from the nearest island, drop anchor off the quay and put their fighters ashore. Kill them all and the raid is beaten off; either way the settlement is safe for five days afterward.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p15.text1: Hats and coats are armour too.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p15.list1: **Hats,** one point each: the {item:pirates_n_ships:pirate_hat}**pirate hat** (three black wool over leather, a bone and leather), the {item:pirates_n_ships:bandana}**bandana** (red wool, string, red wool), the {item:pirates_n_ships:navy_hat}**navy tricorn** (with white wool), the {item:pirates_n_ships:officer_hat}**officer's bicorne** (with a gold nugget), and the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_hat}**captain's hat**, which you only win from a pirate captain.

**The captain's coat, breeches and boots,** in charcoal and gold, and **the officer's coat, breeches and boots,** in navy blue and white: three points for a coat, two for breeches, one for boots. All are crafted from wool, leather and a touch of gold.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.text1: The **kraken** lurks in the deep ocean and rises beside ships, more often at night and in storms. Its tentacles grip the hull and drag her down, beat masts to splinters and sweep the deck; swimmers are pulled under.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.list1: Its eyes are its weak spots: they take triple harm.
Enough harm to a tentacle cuts it, and it lets go until it grows back.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.text2: It leaves a {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**kraken beak** and {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink**, prized by chart makers.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p17.text1: Sharks cruise every ocean a few blocks under the surface. A shark that spots you swimming circles before it charges and bites, and blood in the water drives it into a frenzy. Stay on deck or in a boat and it leaves you alone; climb out and it loses you at once.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text1: In a thunderstorm at sea a **waterspout** may form: a turning column of spray with a low roar. Close to it you, your boat and loose things are pulled in and lifted, and the wind tears set sails down a step every few seconds. Steer clear, or furl first.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text2: In the deep ocean, at any hour, a **whirlpool** may open: a slow ring of foam around a dark centre that draws everything inward. Near its heart it drags boats and swimmers under, and a ship caught there is turned about.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.title: Charts and navigation
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p1.text1: A captain who does not know where he is soon knows where the rocks are. Keep your chart, mark it well, and trust the lead more than your memory.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.text1: Every captain keeps a chart of his own, and it draws itself as you sail: the coasts within about 96 blocks are inked in as you pass, with hatched shallows, sandy beaches and the open sea, where the odd sea serpent lurks. Only the seas of the overworld are charted.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.text2: Craft a {item:pirates_n_ships:chart}**chart** from paper, leather and a feather, and use it to open your map. Or press **M** with the chart in either hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.list1_: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
Right-click to place a marker with a name: X marks the spot, an anchorage, a skull, a port or a danger. Click a marker to rename or remove it.
Your ship shows where you are and which way you head.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**map tile** (eight sticks around a paper) hangs on a wall or lies on a table. Set several side by side in a rectangle, all facing the same way, and they make one board, up to 8 tiles on a side.
