lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text2: **1.** Use any tile with your chart in hand: your chart opens with a frame the shape of the board.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text3: **2.** Drag the frame over the waters you want, pick a zoom, and choose whether your markers go on it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text5: Drawing costs ink: an ink sac or glow ink sac for each tile. A single {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink** pays for eight.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text6: Later, anyone who has charted more can use the board and press **Update**: what they know fills in the blank parchment, what was drawn before stays, and they pay only for the tiles that changed. **New** draws the board afresh at another place or zoom, and **Clear** wipes it; both ask you to click twice. Look at a tile to see who drew it, when, and where. Break a tile and it keeps its piece of the drawing; set it back and the board is whole again.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text1: The lookout in the crow's nest calls in points of the compass from the bow: 32 points to the circle, eight to each quarter.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.list1_: **Two points off the starboard bow:** a little to the right of ahead.
**On the beam:** square off the side.
**Three points abaft the beam:** behind the beam, toward the stern.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text1: Fences on pirate islands sell blank {item:pirates_n_ships:treasure_map}**treasure maps**, and wreck chests hold one now and then. Use a blank map and it marks the nearest buried treasure that no one has yet dug up; if there is none within reach, it stays blank.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text2: While you hold the map it shows the island with a red X and tells you the way: "NW, 340 blocks". At the X, dig about two blocks into the sand and open the chest. Once the treasure is found, every map of it turns grey and keeps as a keepsake, and the next blank map leads somewhere new.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text3: Every pirate island has a chest buried beneath two crossed logs. Dig at the cross.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text1: The ocean floor is strewn with the bones of ships: a broken sloop, a field of scattered cargo, a mast stump with its yard, the stern of something larger. Each holds a chest of ship's stores: doubloons, rum, salted fish, rope, nails, lead shot, now and then a cutlass or a treasure map, rarely kraken ink.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text2: Tall wrecks lie only in deep water; in the shallows you find cargo fields. Take something to let you breathe and see down there.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.title: The ship's inventory
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p1.tex: Every block and item a sea-going hand may need, with a line on each and the chapter that tells the rest.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p2.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**Helm:** launches, steers and takes apart a ship. [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**Yard:** a spar; two on a mast make a square sail. [[pirates_n_ships:sailing|Sailing]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:cleat}**Cleat:** holds a stay, a rope line or a grappling rope.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope}**Rope:** three string; rigs stays and rope lines.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**Sail winch:** works every sail aboard. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**Capstan:** drops and weighs the anchor. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:mooring_ring}**Mooring ring:** catches and holds a grappling hook.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ratlines}**Ratlines:** rope nets for climbing aloft.
{item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**Crow's nest:** the lookout's barrel. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ships_bell}**Ship's bell:** rings when struck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**Bilge pump:** pumps a flooded hold. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hull_patch}**Hull patch:** closes a breach.
{item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**Flagpole:** flies your colours. [[pirates_n_ships:flags|Flags]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:nameplate}**Nameplate:** shows her name.

{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_mermaid}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_lion}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_eagle}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_skull}**Figureheads:** a mermaid, lion, eagle or skull for the bow.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_lantern}**Ship's lantern:** a lantern that burns under water.
{item:pirates_n_ships:stern_window}**Stern window:** shuttered windows for the great cabin.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope_coil}**Rope coil:** coiled rope for the deck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:chart_table}**Chart table:** a captain's table.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**Sea cot:** the captain's bed at sea.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**Hammock:** a bunk for one hand. [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**Boarding plank:** a bridge to an enemy deck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p3.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_crate}**Cargo crate:** 32 stacks of one item. [[pirates_n_ships:trade|Cargo and trade]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:hardtack}**Hardtack,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salted_fish}**salted fish,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salt_pork}**salt pork:** food that never spoils.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rum}**Rum:** cheers a crew and warms a swimmer.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p4.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**Lead shot:** a ball for pistol or musket.
{item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**Swivel gun:** a small gun on a yoke. A station.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p5.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**Bounty proof:** proof of a kill; hand it to a navy officer.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**Ship commission:** an armed sloop earned by rank.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p6.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**Map tile:** a board for a drawn chart.

{item:pirates_n_ships:shipwright_toolkit}**Shipwright's toolkit,** from the {item:pirates_n_ships:carpenters_hammer}**carpenter's hammer,** {item:pirates_n_ships:saw}**saw** and {item:pirates_n_ships:nails}**nails:** joins a broken ship.
{item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**Kraken beak,** {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink:** spoils of the deep.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p7.tex: Every one of them is in the "Pirates 'n' Ships" tab of the creative inventory, with spawn eggs for the folk and beasts of the sea.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.title: The Quartermaster's ledger
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p1.text1: These pages are for the keeper of a server, not for the hand at the wheel. Here are the settings that change how the sea plays, and the orders an operator may give. Every feature has a switch and every strength a value; only the ones a keeper reaches for first are written here.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text1: Open them in game under Mods, then Pirates 'n' Ships, then Config (on a Fabric server with Mod Menu installed). Gameplay settings sit in the server config, which every client receives; how things look and sound sits in each player's client config.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text2: Settings are written as section.name, with the default after the colon.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p3.list1_: assembly.max\_blocks: 2048. The largest ship a helm launches.
assembly.max\_tilt\_degrees: 6, assembly.max\_linear\_speed: 0.3. How still a ship must lie to be taken apart.
assembly.rejoin: the shipwright's toolkit; nails per repair 4, largest piece 200.
ship\_screen.enabled: true. Off, sneak-using the helm takes the ship apart at once.
helm.wheel.drag\_steering: true. Off, the wheel is clicked in thirds.
sailing.sails.yard\_min\_gap 2, yard\_max\_gap 8, yard\_max\_length 15. sailing.sails.dyeing, banners: true.
waves: the sea state; hazards: waterspouts, whirlpools and the kraken (hazards.kraken.enabled).
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p4.list1_: flooding.pump\_enabled, patch\_enabled: true. flooding.pump\_rate: 1 block a second. flooding.pump\_reach: 4.
dry\_hull.flood\_breath: true. Off, flood water inside a hull never drowns.
provisions: rations, spoilage (5 days), scurvy (8 days), rum, the water barrel (16 rations).
survival: cold water and swimming hunger.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p5.list1_: crew.walk.enabled: true. Off, hands take their stations at once.
cannons.npc: what crews do under Fire at will.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p6.list1_: melee.skill\_based\_combat: true. Off, the mod's swords fight like vanilla swords.
firearms.fire\_on\_attack: true. Off, guns fire when right click is released.
cannons: damage 20, reload 100 ticks; cannons.chain\_shot, cannons.grapeshot, cannons.swivel.
combat.cannon\_block\_damage: true. Cannon fire also obeys the mobGriefing game rule and spawn protection.
grapple: rope lengths (32 thrown, grapple.launch 64 from a musket), grapple.hauling, grapple.slide.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p7.list1_: law: crime points, decay, fines (3 a point), bounties (twice the record from 50).
flags\_brig: false colours, surrender, capturing players, escapes. brig: capture at a quarter health, cell size 64.
cargo\_trade: markets, contracts, plunder (fence discount 35 %), port fees (5).
careers, reputation, quests: the rank ladders, standing and the harbour quests.
world.structures: villages, navy outposts, pirate islands, wrecks.
world\_simulation: voyages, convoys, navy patrols, raids, pirate captains at sea.
mobs: pirates, navy, sharks (mobs.shark), the kraken (mobs.kraken), harbour masters, pirate captains.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p8.list1_: /pirates career: your rank, standing and letter of marque.
/pirates rep: your standing with the navy, the pirates and the villagers.
/pirates waves: the sea state where you stand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p9.list1_: /pirates ship forces, info, rigging, templates, place <template> [force] [assemble], orders.
/pirates crew spawn, info, assign, release, order <order>, order course <x> <z> ..., hire <sailor|pirate> [port], dismiss.
/pirates provisions show, advance: a dry run of a crew's stores.
/pirates trade port, open, goods, buy, sell, contracts, contract, weight, plunder, coins, desk bind <port>, desk unbind, desk info.
/pirates law score, crime, last, hostile, fine, bounty list, place, claim, clear.
/pirates brig list, capture, deliver, ransom, pressgang, release.
/pirates career set, letter, ship\_grant; /pirates rep set; /pirates quest offer, complete.
/pirates mob spawn <type> [count], mob debug on|off, mob captain spawn, list, voyage, mob squad info, patrol, return.
/pirates world ports, port nearest, treasure give, factions, patrols, raid chance, raid <port>, voyages.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p10.text1: Ship templates, trade goods and weapon timings are data files under data/<namespace>/pirates\_n\_ships/, and block and item tags decide what never sails (terrain, never\_assemble), what keeps water out (watertight, not\_watertight), which foods keep or cure scurvy, and what may be hoisted (flags). A datapack can replace any of them, or add to the Almanac itself: see the mod's chapter format.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.title: Not yet charted
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p1.text1: An honest chart leaves blank what nobody has sailed. These are the waters this Almanac cannot yet describe, because nobody has built them yet.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p2.list1: **Oars** to move a big ship in a flat calm.
**A ship's logbook** to record your voyages and deeds.
**Paint for the hull,** to dye her planks your own colours.
**A wanted poster** of your own, beyond the chat, the notice board and the rank box.
**Feints of your own** with the sword, and a way to choose the side of your cut and your parry.
**Sounds of their own** for most of the work aboard: until then, the creak of the hull, the shanties and the guns must do.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p2.text1: If you find something in these pages that the sea does not do, or something the sea does that these pages do not tell, the mistake is the Almanac's. Tell whoever keeps your server.
